summary: Unexpected 5xx surge from API gateway during ephemeral sidecar hot-rotate causing runtime overload
description: Issue summary: Between 02:20 and 02:40 UTC on 2026-03-12 we observed a ~6 minute elevated 5xx spike for tenant VeloxAI on prod-us-east. API gateway returned 502/503/504 for ~12% of requests to chat/generate endpoints. Impact: customer facing latency and failed calls, highest throughput tenants impacted. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated capacity pool for VeloxAI, routing through edge cluster edge-us-e1.
impact: Customer VeloxAI saw approximately 12% error rate on generation endpoints for ~6 minutes, causing downstream request retries and degraded UX. No data loss. Multiple support customers reported errors concurrently.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Target VeloxAI's chat/generate endpoint in prod-us-east with sustained 200 rps small payload.
2) Trigger a sidecar hot-rotate on the edge cluster (simulate rolling restart of sidecar proxies).
3) Observe elevated 502/503 rates on the responses for several minutes until accept queue stabilizes.
logs: 2026-03-12T02:23:13Z sidecar proxy[pid=2378]: hot-rotate start, draining connections
2026-03-12T02:23:14Z serving-runtime[pid=4421] WARNING: slow-accept-handshake latency=230ms threads=48 cpu=95%
2026-03-12T02:24:50Z apigw grpc: upstream_reset before first byte for 64 connections
2026-03-12T02:25:05Z autoscaler: ephemeral-init throttled due to prewarm 0->3 scale operation
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: rolling restart of sidecar proxies caused transient accept-queue flush and a wave of half-open connections that were rejected by API gateway.
Correlation found between sidecar hot-rotate and increase in apigw accept_queue drops + an autoscaler prewarm that overlapped the rotation window.
Heap/CPU on serving-runtime spiked during the window, likely due to large number of aborted sessions and retry fanout.
No GPU OOMs or driver resets; NVML logs clean. Runtime thread dumps show blocked accept() syscalls and backlog growth.
Client retry behavior amplified the spike; many clients retried aggressively creating thundering retry pattern.
timeline: 02:20 UTC - Scheduled maintenance: sidecar hot-rotate initiated in edge-us-e1 (tenant-affecting subset).
02:22 UTC - Autoscaler started prewarm for dedicated pool (0->3) coincidentally.
02:23 UTC - apigw accept_queue started dropping connections; 5xx rate climbs.
02:29 UTC - Ops temporarily reduced ingress concurrency for VeloxAI and disabled prewarm; 5xx rate begins to decline.
02:36 UTC - Normal error rates restored; full rollback of hot-rotate completed by 02:45.
mitigation: Immediate: Scoped ingress priority for VeloxAI, reduced per-tenant concurrency, and paused sidecar rotation.
Applied temporary rate-limiter on client retries via edge reject-after-backoff policy.
Disabled autoscaler prewarm overlapping rotations for the affected zone.
resolution: Root cause: timing overlap between sidecar hot-rotate (edge proxy drain) and autoscaler prewarm which produced an accept_queue flush and an upstream runtime CPU spike from retry amplification. Fix: adjust rollout coordination to block autoscaler prewarms during sidecar rotations; implement accept_queue backpressure smoothing in apigw; add jitter to client-side SDK retry backoff recommendations. Changes scheduled for rollout in next minor patch; short-term runbook updated.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add circuit-breaker guard in apigw to reject new tenant traffic gracefully during edge-sidecar drain (owner: infra-team, ETA: 2 weeks).
2) Implement prewarm-rollout interlock so autoscaler prewarm does not overlap proxy rotations (owner: autoscaler-team, ETA: 2 weeks).
3) Update SDK docs with exponential jittered retry guidance and add server-side retry-control headers (owner: SDK/Client platform, ETA: 1 week).
4) Postmortem to be drafted and linked in Confluence (owner: oncall, ETA: 3 days).

public_notes: Customer-facing summary: We observed a short-lived increase in server errors caused by a coordination issue between proxy rollouts and autoscaler prewarm. We have implemented mitigations and will deploy a fix to prevent recurrence. No user data was lost.
